01 / GET STARTED

Run and test locally

The API listens on http://127.0.0.1:3001/api/v1 by default. Configure the Supabase URL and publishable key in apps/api/.env. Start the backend alone for these checks.

Required headers

The publishable key is not a user token. Sign in with an existing registered owner account through Supabase Auth.

Recommended first requests

  1. GET /health to verify the process.
  2. GET /auth/session with the owner token.
  3. GET /health/ready to verify the database.
  4. POST /workspace/initialize.
  5. Create a test company and customer.
  6. Resolve a style, preview a bill, then save it.
The API may run locally while its database is hosted. Every mutation targets the Supabase project configured in the API environment. Use a dedicated test company or staging project.
Complete PowerShell acceptance guide, including sign-in
02 / SYSTEM DESIGN

Architecture and data passing

Thogai uses a Fastify API with TypeScript and Zod, Supabase Auth for identity, PostgreSQL for transactional business rules, and private Supabase Storage for document files.

01 · HTTPClient requestMethod, path, query, JSON body, Bearer token, version or retry key.
02 · APIVerify and validateAuthenticate the registered owner. Validate UUIDs, dates, supported fields, precision, and request shape.
03 · DATABASEAuthorize and transactResolve company scope, lock business records, enforce relationships and lifecycle rules, compute totals.
04 · RESPONSEReturn the contractJSON record, paginated list, aggregate, empty 204, or authorized PDF/CSV bytes.

Business data path

Request → authenticate() → Zod → owner/company lookup → PostgreSQL RPC or RLS query → response

Database functions derive the workspace from the authenticated actor. A company ID supplied in a URL is a filter and reference, never sufficient authorization.

Document generation path

Issue → durable file job → authorized download → lease/claim → snapshot render → private upload → checksum → ready file

Playwright Chromium renders PDFs. File and report jobs currently execute on download requests. Scheduled background workers are a future automation.

Motion design and timing notes

Request, response, and UI responsibilities

A successful UI preview is useful feedback, but stored financial totals come from the database transaction. The browser attaches the owner's access token and record version. The server verifies scope, and PostgreSQL enforces the final constraints. Synthetic JWT labels in this animation are placeholders, never credentials.

How information moves

Deep architecture: modules, checks, transactions and file paths

The health endpoint checks the API process without querying business records. Other paths use only the layers they need; a diagram branch is not an assertion that every API writes data. A token is your temporary sign-in pass. JSON is a structured message containing named fields. An RPC is one named database operation. A transaction means related changes succeed together or roll back together. A cache is a temporary browser copy used to draw the screen.

04 / DATA INTEGRITY
Relationships and company isolation
The map shows the primary billing chain. The complete foreign-key list below includes all composite references, actor references to auth.users, and nullable links.




Entity-owned child records reference scoped parent keys such as (workspace_id, entity_id, id). A customer, style, receipt, or document cannot be attached to another company's records through a valid composite foreign key. Standalone challans may have a free-text recipient and no customer. Linked challans require the invoice's customer.


05 / HTTP CONTRACTS
Every endpoint, input, and output
All paths include /api/v1. GET, POST, PATCH, and DELETE are implemented. HEAD and OPTIONS are framework-generated. Updates use PATCH; there are no PUT routes.






06 / RULES
Validation, authorization, and calculations


How money moves through an invoice
  1. Multiply quantity by unit rate and round line gross to two decimal places.
  2. Add any signed line adjustment and subtract the line's fixed discount.
  3. Allocate the invoice discount proportionally across line bases in integer paise using largest remainder and row-order tie breaking.
  4. Calculate and round applicable tax components per line. Sum line taxable values and tax amounts.
  5. Apply the snapshotted rounding increment and persist reconciled header totals.
  6. Receipt posting locks the invoice and rejects payment above its remaining balance. Reversal retains the original receipt.


Access control
RLS is enabled on application tables. Controlled SECURITY DEFINER operations perform explicit actor/workspace checks and use an empty search path with qualified relations. Direct browser writes to financial records, counters, and audit records are restricted. Historical reads remain available after company archival.
Private files use workspace/company-prefixed object paths. Downloads recheck ownership. Published templates, immutable asset paths, and issued snapshots preserve historical rendering.

08 / TRANSACTIONS
Lifecycle and data-passing contracts


Style resolution
  1. Receive a company ID and entered style number.
  2. Verify registered owner and active company.
  3. Trim outer spaces and uppercase the lookup key.
  4. Insert with conflict handling against the company-scoped normalized unique key.
  5. Read and lock the matching record, rejecting archived matches.
  6. Return the same style UUID for an existing match.
Draft saving resolves nonblank style inputs again in its transaction. Preview rolls these writes back.
Invoice lifecycle
draft → issued → cancelled
Drafts may be changed or deleted with the current version. Issuance locks the draft, validates it, allocates its number, freezes its content, and queues a PDF job. Cancellation requires a reason and reversal of active receipts. It retains the number and original financial contents.
unpaid / partially_paid / paid and overdue are calculated states, separate from lifecycle.
Challan lifecycle
draft → issued → cancelled
Challans use independent numbering. A standalone recipient is allowed. An optional invoice link must match company and customer. Received-by evidence is a separate immutable acknowledgement so the issued document remains unchanged.
File and export jobs
pending → processing → ready / failed
Lease expiry and claim tokens protect completion. Retrying failed work does not reissue a document. Report exports materialize data and date cutoffs before rendering. An expired report requires a new request. Current processing is triggered by authorized download calls.


Financial reporting cutoffs
Billing uses invoice business dates. Collections use receipt dates. Outstanding includes earlier unpaid invoices. Historical reporting uses both a business asOf date and recorded timestamp cutoff. Later cancellations and reversals must not erase earlier balances. Quantities stay grouped by unit.


09 / RECOVERY
Errors, concurrency, and retries
Error envelopes differ across existing handlers. Read error and treat issues, code, and requestId as optional. Validation issue messages depend on the failed fields and the Zod version.


  • On stale-version conflict, refetch the record and reconcile the edit. Do not overwrite with an old version.
  • Retry a payment with the exact same body and the exact same Idempotency-Key.
  • Reuse the original draft UUID on creation retry. A new UUID means a new draft.
  • A live job claim returns conflict. Retry the download after the active generation finishes or its lease expires.
  • Failed or expired-lease jobs can be requeued through retry endpoints. Completed files are reused.
  • Keep issued document numbers permanently reserved through every correction.


10 / VERIFICATION
Evidence and local acceptance
Use your owner account, a dedicated test company, and representative business data to test successful authenticated HTTP requests, file uploads/downloads, deployment Chromium, and network failure recovery. Automated route coverage verifies that every implemented endpoint is documented; it does not establish that every possible live input has been tested.


Automation opportunities
  • Background PDF generation and bounded failed-job retries.
  • Draft autosave when frontend integration is authorized.
  • Opt-in payment reminders and receipt confirmations.
  • Daily owner summaries and scheduled monthly exports.
  • Storage retention cleanup and isolated backup/restore verification.
Scheduled workers and outbound notifications are separate features. The implemented job tables and claim APIs provide the foundation.
